citation.authors: George MD, McGill NK, Baker JF

cited_by.title: Starting training, rest days and recovery

record.population: 10,096 non-pregnant US adults aged 20 and over, NHANES 2011-2014
record.design: Cross-sectional survey; creatine kinase compared by sex and race-ethnicity, excluding recent strenuous exercise
record.finding: Black race was strongly associated with creatine kinase: the odds of an abnormal result were 5.08 times higher (95% CI 3.65-7.08) for Black women and 8.39 times higher (6.11-11.52) for Black men. Body size and composition mattered but did not explain the racial difference. The 97.5th percentile was 382 in white men and 1001 in black men; 295 in white women and 487 in black women.
record.note: Healthy-population reference ranges, not an exercise recovery study. Self-reported race-ethnicity.
